record.original_question: Let V_{d1,...,dk} be the Segre-Veronese variety of partially symmetric rank-one tensors in P(S^{d1}V1 ⊗ ··· ⊗ S^{dk}Vk). For each r, the r-th secant variety σ_r(V_{d1,...,dk}) has expected dimension min{r dim(V_{d1,...,dk}) + r - 1, ambient dimension}. Which Segre-Veronese varieties are r-defective (that is, have secant variety of smaller than expected dimension), and what are the actual dimensions of their secant varieties?

evidence.quote: Problem 1. Classify defective Segre-Veronese varieties and determine their dimension.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k\ge 1$ be an integer, and for each $i=1,\dots,k$ let $V_i$ be a complex vector space of dimension $n_i+1\ge 2$, and let $d_i\ge 1$ be a positive integer. Consider the Segre–Veronese variety
$$V_{d_1,\dots,d_k}\;\subset\;\mathbb{P}\bigl(S^{d_1}V_1\otimes\cdots\otimes S^{d_k}V_k\bigr),$$
defined as the image of $\mathbb{P}(V_1)\times\cdots\times\mathbb{P}(V_k)$ under the embedding given by the line bundle $\mathcal{O}(d_1,\dots,d_k)$; equivalently, it parametrizes partially symmetric rank-one tensors $v_1^{\otimes d_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_k^{\otimes d_k}$ up to scalar. Let $N=\dim\mathbb{P}(S^{d_1}V_1\otimes\cdots\otimes S^{d_k}V_k)$ and let $n=\dim V_{d_1,\dots,d_k}=\sum_i n_i$. For an integer $r\ge 1$, the $r$-th secant variety $\sigma_r(V_{d_1,\dots,d_k})$ is the Zariski closure of the union of linear spans of $r$ points of $V_{d_1,\dots,d_k}$. Its expected dimension is
$$\operatorname{expdim}\sigma_r(V_{d_1,\dots,d_k})=\min\{\,r\,n+r-1,\;N\,\}.$$
The variety $V_{d_1,\dots,d_k}$ is called $r$-defective if $\dim\sigma_r(V_{d_1,\dots,d_k})$ is strictly smaller than this expected dimension.

Problem. Classify all tuples $(n_1,\dots,n_k;\,d_1,\dots,d_k;\,r)$ for which the Segre–Veronese variety $V_{d_1,\dots,d_k}$ is $r$-defective, and in each defective case determine the exact value of $\dim\sigma_r(V_{d_1,\dots,d_k})$.
artifact.status_search_result: A complete classification is not known. For pure Veronese varieties ($k=1$) the Alexander–Hirschowitz theorem gives a full answer, and many partial results exist (e.g. Abo–Brambilla conjectural list for two factors, non-defectivity results of Galuppi–Oneto and recent work showing non-defectivity when all $d_i\ge 3$ or in asymptotic regimes), but the general classification problem for arbitrary $k$ and arbitrary multi-degrees remains open, with new defective examples still being discovered for three- and four-factor cases.

status_evidence.title: Non-defectivity of Segre-Veronese varieties
status_evidence.snippet: Segre-Veronese varieties are never secant defective if each degree is at least three.
status_evidence.claim: Recent partial result; general classification not stated as complete.

status_evidence.title: New examples of defective secant varieties of Segre-Veronese varieties
status_evidence.snippet: New defective examples in three- and four-factor cases.
status_evidence.claim: New defective cases continue to be discovered, indicating the classification remains open.

status_evidence.title: On secant defectiveness and identifiability of Segre–Veronese varieties
status_evidence.claim: Problem treated via partial results only.
